CONFIDENTIAL — CORPORATE DATA SECURITY AUDIT REPORT

Report Reference: AUD-2026-778341
Prepared by: Meridian Compliance Partners LLC
Audit Period: March 2, 2026 to March 14, 2026
Lead Auditor: Rebecca Sinclair (Auditor License No. CPA-8827104)
Client Organization: Northbridge Financial Holdings Inc.
Client Contact: Daniel Okafor, Chief Information Security Officer
Contact Email: daniel.okafor@northbridgefh.com
Contact Phone: (312) 555-0148

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report documents the findings of a comprehensive data security audit conducted at Northbridge Financial Holdings Inc., headquartered at 4820 Lakeshore Drive, Suite 1100, Chicago, Illinois 60611. The audit was commissioned following an internal data access review and covered personnel records, customer account files, and network access logs maintained between January 1, 2026 and February 28, 2026. The audit team also reviewed retention policies governing archived records stored at the offsite facility located at 900 Industrial Parkway, Bedford Park, Illinois 60501. The scope of the engagement was defined jointly by the client's compliance department and the audit firm during a kickoff meeting held in the first week of the audit period, and it was later expanded to include a review of third-party vendor access controls after preliminary findings suggested that external service accounts had broader database permissions than originally documented.

2. METHODOLOGY

The audit team applied a risk-based sampling methodology consistent with industry standard frameworks for financial services data governance. Personnel and customer records were selected using stratified random sampling across departments and account tiers, ensuring that both high-privilege administrative accounts and standard customer-facing accounts were represented in the review. Network access logs were analyzed using automated anomaly detection tools cross-referenced against the corporate VPN allowlist, and any login event originating outside the expected IP ranges was flagged for manual review by a senior analyst. Interviews were conducted with department heads to confirm that documented access control policies matched actual operational practice, and discrepancies between policy and practice were recorded as separate findings distinct from the technical control gaps identified in the log review.

4. NETWORK ACCESS LOG FINDINGS

During the audit period, the security operations center flagged several login events originating from outside the corporate VPN range for review.

An anomalous login attempt was recorded from IP address 198.51.100.42 on March 4, 2026, targeting the account of employee Jonathan Marsh. A second anomalous login was traced to IP address 203.0.113.77 on March 9, 2026, associated with a failed access attempt on the customer database using the credentials of Elena Vasquez. A third event originated from IP address 192.0.2.155 on March 11, 2026, and was linked to an unrecognized device attempting to access the fraud case management system under case reference FRD-2026-005512. A fourth event was logged from IP address 198.51.100.90 on March 12, 2026, involving a login to the archived records system using the credentials of Natalie Ferreira.

5. VENDOR AND THIRD-PARTY ACCESS

The audit also reviewed third-party vendor access granted to CloudGuard Analytics Inc., whose designated account representative is Kevin Truong, reachable at kevin.truong@cloudguardanalytics.com or (415) 555-0140. Vendor access credentials were issued under service account ID SVC-CGA-0091 and were last rotated on February 20, 2026. A second vendor, Harborline Data Services LLC, was granted read-only access under service account ID SVC-HDS-0044, managed by representative Olivia Grant, who can be reached at olivia.grant@harborlinedata.com.

6. FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

The audit identified several high-priority findings, documented under internal tracking numbers FND-2026-1001, FND-2026-1002, FND-2026-1003, and FND-2026-1004. It is recommended that Northbridge Financial Holdings Inc. enforce mandatory multi-factor authentication for all remote access sessions, restrict database query permissions for the Fraud Prevention Unit, and rotate all vendor service account credentials on a ninety-day cycle going forward. In addition, the audit team recommends that the organization implement automated alerting for any login attempt originating from an IP address outside the approved corporate range, rather than relying solely on periodic manual log review, since the anomalous events described in Section 4 were only identified retrospectively during this engagement. Management should also consider tightening the offboarding process for departing employees to ensure that credentials are revoked within twenty-four hours of separation, and should require annual re-certification of all vendor access grants rather than allowing them to persist indefinitely once initially approved.

7. RISK RATING SUMMARY

Each finding in this report has been assigned a qualitative risk rating of High, Medium, or Low based on the likelihood of exploitation and the potential impact on customer or employee data. Findings related to unmonitored external login attempts and overly broad vendor database permissions were rated High due to the direct exposure of sensitive personal and financial information. Findings related to documentation gaps between stated policy and observed practice were generally rated Medium, reflecting a lower immediate risk but a meaningful control weakness that could compound over time if left unaddressed. No findings in this engagement were rated Low, as the sample review consistently surfaced conditions warranting remediation within the current fiscal quarter.

7. SIGN-OFF

This report was reviewed and approved for release by Rebecca Sinclair on March 15, 2026. Questions regarding this report should be directed to Meridian Compliance Partners LLC at audits@meridiancompliance.com or by calling the main office at (212) 555-0199.
